execution_status: Per-run private reports record actual checks. The declared scenarios are not service parity or proof that an arbitrary host or guest meets the native prerequisites.
module_interface: run(args, root: Path, endpoint: str, terraform, variables: dict, stages: list) -> (verify(endpoint=None), cleanup(endpoint=None))

notes: Paths are explicit operator inputs, not download, installation, image creation, firmware discovery or build commands. Select existing matching firmware and a prepared guest; keep the input image unchanged.

Use an existing short private persistent work-parent owned by the controller identity. The runner uses a shorter ebs-controls root name; the complete vm-<digest>/qmp.sock path must still fit Linux's 107-byte socket-path limit.
The root runner defaults to s3,dynamodb; EBS is opt-in through --services ebs or a comma-separated list including ebs.
--guest-instance-type defaults to t3.small and consumes actual host RAM/vCPU. Select an available compatible x86_64 instance type only after provisioning its host capacity.

No native AWS endpoint or payment is used. API endpoints are explicit loopback; provider account discovery remains enabled. STS, IAM, KMS, EC2 and EBS dependency endpoints are all explicit. No S3 dependency is introduced by the EBS module.

The native EC2 controller listens on 0.0.0.0 at the exact owned port so its network toolkit can reach it. The SDK, Terraform and readiness endpoints remain explicit 127.0.0.1; the same listener rule applies after controller reopen.

Provider6.68.0 has no ebs endpoint argument. Terraform EBS volume and snapshot resources use its explicit ec2 endpoint; the real EBS Direct bootstrap and block readers use explicit loopback SDK clients.

guest_image: Required existing raw full-disk Linux x86_64 HVM image with the selected firmware bootloader and NVMe root support; QCOW2, a filesystem tarball or an invented AMI ID is rejected/not substituted

All guest packages must already exist; user-data does not install software or fetch anything from the Internet

User-data starts an authenticated Python HTTP consumer on TCP8765. Only the owned subnet gateway /32 is admitted by its security group. The host initiates HTTP to the exact Terraform-produced private IP; guest-to-controller callback routing is unnecessary.

native_owner_contract.authority: Authoritative independently hydrated qcow2 disks are owned by EBS. EC2 attachments realize their exact paths via QMP, not a second mutable disk store. NVMe hardware serial is the terminal volume ID with hyphens removed.
native_owner_contract.resize: Existing native owner supports detached qemu-img resize and attached QMP block_resize. This fixture exercises only detached growth 1->2GiB and verifies BLKGETSIZE64 after real reattachment, not filesystem expansion or online guest rescan.
native_owner_contract.snapshot: Existing volume-derived snapshot owner captures the actual native disk at admission and publishes immutable EBS Direct blocks. This fixture takes a cold detached snapshot and asserts both immutable source volume ID and source size.
native_owner_contract.network_observation: Native TAP observation queries only the exact instance-derived device. It does not enumerate all host interfaces. The64KiB helper guard remains in force; a missing kernel sysfs device is normal before create or after remove, and errors reading an existing device remain failures.
native_owner_contract.native_effects: One service-owned native flight copies blocks and runs disk effects outside the shared scheduler drain. Eligible metadata heads still advance in the calling drain. The two existing snapshot and volume queues keep their own head order: a native head can delay later work in the same queue, but does not block the other queue or joined services.
native_owner_contract.shutdown_and_recovery: Shutdown cancels and joins the native flight. Native callers use a private context-cancelable gate, so a canceled EC2 worker does not wait for uncanceled EBS work during consumer-first shutdown. Committed block rows are the resume cursor after reopen. Every hydration write and final publication checks the admitted volume incarnation and source.
native_owner_contract.timing: Module-local ticker advances the persisted shared manual clock by 1s every 0.5s only while EBS operations/provider waits run. Native disk/guest readiness requires actual serial, requested byte capacity and independent nonzero binary reads; API running/completed metadata alone is insufficient.

Ordinary and refresh-only no-change plans without ignored drift; same independent native bytes, capacity, isolation and immutable source IDs checked again by root after SQLite/controller reopen
Terraform-owned guest/network/volumes/snapshot/IAM destroy and explicit owned bootstrap AMI deregistration/snapshot deletion; source-image SHA256 remains unchanged

state_and_failure_safety: Owned root/module directories mode0700, tfvars and captured Terraform command logs mode0600; sensitive outputs are consumed from captured JSON and never echoed.
Bootstrap snapshot and AMI IDs are recorded privately as soon as accepted, before later work can fail. Every run failure enters the same owned Terraform destroy and bootstrap cleanup path.

Before strict plans, each initial/reopen payload phase records actual decoded guest and EBS Direct SHA256, byte lengths, device serials, owned IDs and unchanged input image SHA256 in a private native-evidence receipt.

Both refresh-only and ordinary strict plans retain their saved binary plan and command logs. Only exit2 with explicit no-change stdout and saved-plan JSON containing no resource/drift/output changes is retained as a typed strict-plan failure; it remains terminal, but permits the independent SQLite/controller reopen payload phase before ordinary cleanup. Any other behavior failure stops immediately.
Prior Terraform state and prior .backup bytes are saved privately before state removal. Failed import restores both before normal destroy, preventing orphaning caused by a lost state binding.

Teardown failure is a failure, not success or readiness. Retain the printed owned directory, SQLite database and native EC2 directory together for diagnosis; never remove them to silence a failed destroy.
The image is opened read-only, never converted/resized/mounted/modified by this fixture; unchanged SHA256 is checked after native lifecycle and controller reopen.
coverage_rule: These entries describe implemented exercises, not observed support. All inventory/default evidence remains unverified until the root runner completes actual independent native consumers and records passed stages. No whole-EC2, whole-IAM, arbitrary image, host installer, metadata-only readiness, zero-block proof or performance support claim.
